ALLEGEZTREFT OF A SHIRT.--At Lymm Police Court, on Wednesday, before Mr. Dewhurst, two Northwich labourers named Michael Fadner and Edward Shaugnessy were charged with stealing a shirt, value is 63, the pro- perty of Richard Finn, of High Legh. The prosecutor did not appear to give evidence against them, and they were consequently discharged. NARROW El/CAPE OF DR. Fox FROM Dnowinna.—On liSattarday afternoon, Dr. Fox, the Medical Officer of Health, ibad a very narrow escape from drowning. Whilst skating I.with a number of friends the ice gave way, and he was im- mersed in the water. A ladder which was on the spot was thrown to the doctor, but be tray unable to hold on to it. A young man named Peter John Jackson then went to his help, and eventually succeeded in rescuing the doctor from his perilous position. Since the accident Dr. Fox has been mash indisposed. NEW GRAMMAR SCEDOL.—A large and handsome build- ing has been erected at Lymm at a coat of between £3OOO and' £4OOO by the governors of a foundation known as the Lymm Grammar School. The building has been erected on a piece of ground presented by Mr. v•Dewhurst, of Beech- woed; Lynam, and will be provided with all the appurten- ances necessary for a school of its character. The erection of the school is the revival of an old trust that has been of great service in the past. The appointment of a master is under consideration. _ . .

SUDDEN DEATH —On Saturday, Mr. Edge, district coroner, held an inquest at the Railway Hotel, Leigh, con- cerning the death of Sarah Leather, who died suddenly the previous Wednesday, at the house of her son-in-law, John Blaine, bricklayer, Bedford-street, Leigh.—Blaine deposed that deceased was the wife of Richard Leather, master fus- tian cutter, Lymm. She was at his house on a visit, but Dr. Gallim3r,, of Lymm, had warned her that she ought not to leave home —Harriet Blanc, daughter of last witness, said slarrheard a fall, and found deceased lying on her back In thekitchen. She ran for a doctor, but deceased was dead before Dr. Hall arrived.—A verdict of "Death from natural canna" was returned.

div.head: LOCAL BOARD MEETING.
div.p: LOCAL BOARD MEETING.

The ordinary monthly mestingof this Board was held at the office at Lymm on Thursday evening, under the presidency of Mr. Cameron. There were also present— Messrs. Dewhurst, Rogers, Thotnason, Callender, Appleton, Wooly, Forster, and Gibbon; Ridgway (clerk), and Mort (inspector of nuisances).—The Chairman read the report of the Surveyor, which stated that a number of surface repairs had been effected in various parts of the district. It also.callrd attention to the necessity for some broken material to be obtained to make good the road surface along the line of the recently constructed sewers in Thel- wall-lane.—The report of the Stnitary Inspector, also read by the Chairman, stated that during last month special attention was paid to the condition of the sewer along Newfield and Eagle Brow. Variona sewers in the district had been regularly flushed, and the bene- ficial effects resulting therefrom were such as to suggest the desirability of extending the flushing as far as , possible to all the severs. Special attention bad also been given to the scavenging requirements of the district, and the privies and ashpits of atout 90 houses had been thoroughly cleansed. It was hoped that daring the course of the pre- sent month the systematic scavenging of the district would be on a satisfactory basis. Disinfection had been carried out when fever CON 9 had occurred, and he was glad to re- port that the epidemic was disappearing.—A conversa- tional discussion followed regarding the sanitary arrange- ments of the village, after which the reports were adopted, as were items of cecesssary expenditure.—The sewage farm report yea') read and adopted, and it was resolved to adver- tise fora quantity of willow setts —lt was also decided, on the motion of Mr. Rogers, stconded by Mr. Dewhurst, that la new safe be purchased.

WARRINGTON PEOPLE'S COLLEGE.
DRAWING EXAMINATION.

The report of the drawing examination held in connection with the science and art department on the 12th November last, has just been received by the secretary, Mr. Edward Milner, and is as follows:—" The total number of exercises examined was 467. Of these 51 in the first grade and 10 in the second grade are marke4 ' excellent ' and receive cer- tificates and pr•zes ; 161 in the first grade and 29 in the second grade are marked 'good' and receive certificates, and 177 are marked 'fair.' Only 39 fail to satisfy the examiners.

The principal successful scholars are given below:— First Grade Freehand, Excellent—William H. Ashcroft, Thomas Basketter, Charles H. Broadhurst, Joseph N. Cas- sidy, John Thomas Owen Chidlaw, Edward Hall Coates, Wilmot G. Cresskill, Richard Dainteth, Arthur J. Dendy, Ethel Fair, Abraham Fenton, Robert Lionel A. Galliers, Harry Gaunt, Arthur Gibson, George T. Heaton, Lucy Jones, Annie B. Lawrenson, Henry Leonard, Louisa I Phillips, Frank Podmore, George A. The prizes awarded by the Science and Art Department for excellence in the first grade consist of drawing boards and T squares, colours or compasses. Those in the second grade are chosen from a list of valuable books, boxes of in- struments, or water colours.
France is preparing to send reinforcements to Tomlin speedily. A BritiA protectorate has been proclaimed over the whole coast of Pondoland.

THEFT AT ORFORD.—On Wednesday, at Warrington County Petty Sessions, Joseph Higginson and Mary Hig- ginson, man, and wife, were charged with stealing two pairs of sheets, five pillow slips, two aprons, one sheet, one ninht- dress, and one towel, the property of Sarah Cane, of 23D, Wiuwick-road, Orford, in March last. Ann Higginson, mother of the male prisoner, was charrd with receiving the same. Joseph Higginson and his wife lodgefis with the prosecutrix, whe left the house for a short time, leaving the articles in question in a box. Subsequently, after the two prisoners had left her house, she discovered that the box had been broken into, and the articles abstracted). On in- formation being given to the police, it was found4hat the property bad been pledged in Warrington by Ann- Higgin- son, who, on being apprehended, said that her sonlywile had given it her to pledge. She now adhered to that statement, and the other prisoners pleaded guilty. The Benah found the case proved against all three, and sent them to prison for a month.

INSANITARY PROPERTY.—At the Borough Court on Mon- day, Cephas Duckworth, secretary for the Harporhey Per- manent Beaefit Building Society, was summoned at the in- stance of the Warrington Corporation in respect tc a num- ber of houses in Hardy-street, which it was allegrel•were in such an insanitary state as to be unfit for habitation.—Mr. Wellhead, from the office of the town clerk, appeared to prosecute, and said that he was instructed that the case was such a flagrant one that they asked for a penalty, and that an order should be made for the premises to be closed until rendered habitable.—lnspector Norman gave evidence as to the condition of the houses, and Dr. Gomel!, medical officer of health, said that he was strongly of oplaion that there was not one of the houses specified which RT.-9 fit for a human being to live in.—The defendant said that receetly a considerable amount bad been spent in repairing the pro- perty, and added that it was a monstrous perversion of tbe truth to say that the houses were not tenantable. He, how- ever, said that he would bring the matter before the mana- gers of the Society as soon as possible, and he had no doubt that the matter would be attended to.—The case was adjourned for fourteen days for defendant to take measures to make the houses habitable. PADGATE INDUSTRIAL SCHOOLS.—Last evening week the annual distribution of prizes to the boys and Orls at Pad- gate Industrial Schools took place. On behalf of the scholars he begged to than./ those who had contributed so readily to the fond for tte purchase of the prizes. They had collected £l6 15s. of which Mt las 61 had been spent. The money which Lad been spent had enabled them to buy a prize for every boy and girl in the school, but the awardee,of course, ranged according to merit. The prizes were worth from 5e down- wards: and he would call upon Mr. Derbyshire to present them. (Applause.)—Mr. Derbyshire eaid that the Rae. G. F. THE ATTEMPT TO MURDER Two CHILDREN —The hear- I big of the charge against Evelyn Redstone, servant girl, , accused of the attempted murder of her master's two chil- dren in the Thames, and subuquent attempted suicide, was resumed at Richmond, Surrey, on Friday, when further evidence was given. The accused was committed for trial at the Old Bailey. PALTER Luereetcs.—The Local Government Board have ad- dressed a circular letter to all Boards of Guardians through- out the Country, in which they state that they have received a eommunication from the Commissioners in Lunacy, in which it is suggested that an important proportion of the pauper lunatics in County Asylums might be adequately tend more economically provided for in the Workhouses. The Commissiomers have furnished returns of cases con- sidered suitable for Workhouses, and the Board request , Guardians to endeavour to carry out the necessary trans- fers. EGYPTIAN FINANCE. PARIS, FRIDAY—The Gazette Diploinatique of to-day states that the French counter proposals regarding the Egyptian question, which are expected to be presented, about the middle of January, will have an exclusively financial character. It will be proposed to issue a loan ot £2,000,000 at 31 per cent, which would be collectively guaranteed by the Powers. TH.E. SOUDAN EXPEDITION.—CAPTURE OF CONVOYS. CIDER!. WELLS, JAN. 3. On Saturday afternoon the scouts cap- tured a convoy of merchandise on its way from Metemmeh to Merawi. The convoy consisted of a number of camels and donkeys accompanied by four natives, who stated that they left Metemmeh on January let, when a detachment of General Gordon's troops was still at Shendy. They estima- ted the Mandi's force at Metemmeh at about 2,000 men. On Sunday Major Kitchener, Colonels Swale and Bonhain, Captain Dawson, and two corporals of Hussars, while reconnoitring in the direction of the Abu Ralf& Well met a small party of natives with camels and asses laden with grain. These they captured, and while returning with them to the camp they sighted an their right a large oonvoy of about seventy camels with fifty natives. Major Kitchener and his party at once galloped after them, shout- ing at the top of their voices.
